description: Compile a LaTeX document, render a page to a PNG you can see, and map a point or a text anchor back to the exact source line. Use this whenever someone describes a page visually — a table style, a rule to remove, spacing, a line running into the margin, a figure that is too large — and before saying a layout change is done. Note that `page` is the PDF page index, not the number printed on the page.

audit.description: Audit every page for layout regressions against the previous audit of this document: pages that stop short, pages that start low, nearly empty pages — but only the ones this edit introduced. Run it after changing a whole class of pages (captions, headers, spacing).

auditBlankMm.description: How deep a hole at the foot of a page must be (mm) before the audit calls it one. Defaults to 30.

compare.description: Path to an earlier PDF of the same document. The page is diffed against it and a before image is rendered.

engine.description: auto | xelatex | lualatex | pdflatex | latexmk | tectonic. Defaults to auto, which picks from what the document uses.

file.description: Path to the main .tex file (absolute, or relative to the current directory).

fresh.description: Ignore the build cache and compile from scratch. Use only if you suspect the cache is stale.

page.description: PDF page to render, 1-based. Omit when using `text`, which finds the page itself.

pointX.description: X of a point on the page, together with pointY. Feed back the bbox of a previous diff to inspect what changed.

pointY.description: Y of the same point, in PDF points from the top-left corner of the page.

sequence.description: Check reading order for numbered labels with this prefix (e.g. '图' or 'Figure'). An inversion is what a figure that became a float while its neighbours stayed inline causes: the reader turns the page to see 图 3-4 before 图 3-3.

text.description: A short string visible on the page (a caption, a heading, a unique phrase). Resolves to its source file:line and page.

name: latex_look
title: See what a LaTeX page actually looks like
